kids.n: Ṭawāf begins and ends at the Black Stone. Keep the Ka‘bah on your left and complete seven circuits outside Ḥijr Ismā‘īl.

text.value: Ṭawāf begins and ends at the Black Stone. Keep the Ka‘bah on your left and complete seven circuits outside Ḥijr Ismā‘īl.

props.text: Right shoulder uncovered (idtibā‘)
Upper sheet passes under the right arm and over the left shoulder

props.description: Short, quick strides in the first three circuits, only where it harms no one.
props.title: Ramal — brisk walk

props.description: Walk calmly for the remaining four circuits.
props.title: Normal pace

props.text: Women walk at a normal pace in all seven circuits and keep both shoulders covered.
Black Stone — start and end each circuit here
Yemeni corner — touch it if you can, without kissing or pointing
Ḥijr Ismā‘īl — walk outside it; it is part of the Ka‘bah
Move counter-clockwise, keeping the Ka‘bah on your left

props.description: Pass the upper sheet under the right armpit and over the left shoulder, leaving the right shoulder bare — for the whole of this Ṭawāf only.
props.title: Idtibā‘ (men only)

props.description: Walk briskly with short steps in the first three circuits; walk normally in the remaining four.
props.title: Ramal (men only)

props.description: Face the Black Stone, marked by a green light on the wall. Touch or kiss it if you can; otherwise point your right hand towards it and say “Allāhu Akbar”.
props.title: Starting point

props.description: Stay outside the semi-circular wall of Ḥijr Ismā‘īl — a circuit walked through it does not count.
props.title: Boundary

kids.n: Between the Yemeni corner & Black Stone

text.value: Between the Yemeni corner & Black Stone

props.translation: “Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
props.transliteration: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā hasanatan wa fil-ākhirati hasanatan wa qinā ʿadhāban-nār.
props.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ

props.text: For the rest of Ṭawāf, make du‘ā freely in your own language, remember Allāh and recite the Qur’ān — there are no fixed words for each circuit.

kids.n: The crowd is too dense to reach the Black Stone. What do you do?

text.value: The crowd is too dense to reach the Black Stone. What do you do?

kids.n: In which circuits do men perform Ramal?

text.value: In which circuits do men perform Ramal?

props.text: All seven circuits
The first three circuits only
Only between the two green lights

kids.n: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

text.value: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

kids.n: After the seventh circuit, men cover the right shoulder again. Pray two rak‘ahs behind Maqām Ibrāhīm if you can, then drink Zamzam.

text.value: After the seventh circuit, men cover the right shoulder again. Pray two rak‘ahs behind Maqām Ibrāhīm if you can, then drink Zamzam.

props.text: The Ka‘bah
Maqām Ibrāhīm — the Station of Ibrāhīm
Pray behind it, so the Maqām is between you and the Ka‘bah
Men: cover the right shoulder before praying — idṭibā‘ ends with Ṭawāf.
Drink with your right hand, facing the Qiblah if you can
Zamzam coolers are placed throughout the Masjid
Make du‘ā as you drink — “Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for.” (Sunan Ibn Mājah)

props.description: Men re-cover the right shoulder as soon as the seventh circuit ends.
props.title: Cover the shoulder

props.description: Behind Maqām Ibrāhīm if possible. If it is crowded, pray anywhere in the Masjid — never in the path of those doing Ṭawāf.
props.title: Where to pray

props.description: Drink to your fill. Some also pour a little over the head, as reported from the Prophet — this is optional, not a rite of ‘Umrah.
props.title: Drinking Zamzam

props.translation: “And take the Station of Ibrāhīm as a place of prayer.”

props.text: The Prophet recited this verse as he approached the Maqām after Ṭawāf, then prayed two rak‘ahs (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim).

kids.n: You have prayed the two rakʿahs and drunk Zamzam. What comes next, before Saʿī?

text.value: You have prayed the two rakʿahs and drunk Zamzam. What comes next, before Saʿī?

kids.n: Which sūrahs are recommended in these two rakʿahs?

text.value: Which sūrahs are recommended in these two rakʿahs?

props.text: Al-Mulk and Yā Sīn
Al-Kāfirūn, then Al-Ikhlāṣ
Al-Falaq and An-Nās

props.explanation: After Al-Fātiḥah, recite Al-Kāfirūn in the first rak‘ah and Al-Ikhlāṣ in the second (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim).
props.title: Not quite — keep going

kids.n: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

text.value: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

kids.n: Sa‘ī begins at Aṣ-Ṣafā. On your first approach, recite the verse, then climb, face the Ka‘bah and remember Allāh.

text.value: Sa‘ī begins at Aṣ-Ṣafā. On your first approach, recite the verse, then climb, face the Ka‘bah and remember Allāh.

props.translation: “Indeed, aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allāh.”
props.arabic: إِنَّ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ

props.translation: “I begin with what Allāh began with.”

props.description: Climb Aṣ-Ṣafā until you can see it, if you are able.
props.title: Face the Ka‘bah

props.description: As in supplication — not as in the takbīr of prayer.
props.title: Raise your hands in du‘ā

props.description: Say the dhikr below three times, making your own du‘ā after the first and second.
props.title: Remembrance three times

props.description: After the third time, descend and begin the first lap.
props.title: Walk towards Al-Marwah

props.description: The verse and “Abda’u bimā bada’allāhu bih” are said once only — on the first approach to Aṣ-Ṣafā.
props.title: One-time recitation

props.description: Repeat the dhikr three times on the hill, with personal du‘ā after the first and second.
props.title: Remembrance pattern

props.description: Raise your hands as in du‘ā while facing the Ka‘bah; there is no pointing towards it.
props.title: Raising the hands

props.description: Wuḍū’ is recommended for Sa‘ī but, according to most scholars, not a condition.
props.title: Purity

props.translation: “Allāh is the Greatest (three times). There is none worthy of worship but Allāh alone, without partner; His is the dominion and His is all praise, and He has power over all things. There is none worthy of worship but Allāh alone; He fulfilled His promise, gave victory to His servant, and alone defeated the confederates.”
props.transliteration: Allāhu Akbar (×3). Lā ilāha illallāhu wahdahu lā sharīka lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa ʿalā kulli shayʾin qadīr. Lā ilāha illallāhu wahdah, anjaza waʿdah, wa nasara ʿabdah, wa hazamal-ahzāba wahdah.
props.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ

kids.n: As-Ṣafā is too crowded to climb. Is your Saʿī still valid?

text.value: As-Ṣafā is too crowded to climb. Is your Saʿī still valid?

kids.n: How many times is the verse recited at As-Ṣafā during Saʿī?

text.value: How many times is the verse recited at As-Ṣafā during Saʿī?

props.text: At the start of every lap
Once only, on the first approach
Every time you reach Al-Marwah

kids.n: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

text.value: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

kids.n: Sa‘ī is seven laps, starting at Aṣ-Ṣafā and ending at Al-Marwah. Remember Allāh throughout; men jog between the green lights.

text.value: Sa‘ī is seven laps, starting at Aṣ-Ṣafā and ending at Al-Marwah. Remember Allāh throughout; men jog between the green lights.

props.text: Aṣ-Ṣafā — lap 1 starts here
Green lights — men jog briskly between them
Al-Marwah — lap 7 ends here
Men: jog between the two green lights without pushing or harming anyone.
Women walk at a normal pace for the whole course, including the green light zone.

props.description: Ṣafā to Marwah is one lap; Marwah back to Ṣafā is the second. The seventh lap ends at Al-Marwah.
props.title: Counting laps

props.description: Each time you reach Ṣafā or Marwah, face the Ka‘bah and repeat the remembrance and du‘ā, as on your first ascent.
props.title: At each hill

props.description: You may rest or use a wheelchair if needed; keep the laps going one after another without a long break.
props.title: Resting

props.description: Your Sa‘ī ends at Al-Marwah. Next, shave or trim your hair to leave Ihrām.
props.title: After lap seven

props.text: There are no fixed words between the hills — make du‘ā freely, remember Allāh, recite the Qur’ān and seek forgiveness.

kids.n: You lose count of your laps. What do you do?

text.value: You lose count of your laps. What do you do?

kids.n: Who jogs between the two green lights?

text.value: Who jogs between the two green lights?

props.text: Both men and women
Men only, without harming others
Only pilgrims performing Ḥajj

kids.n: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

text.value: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

kids.n: The final rite is cutting the hair. Once done, you leave Ihrām — its restrictions are lifted and your ‘Umrah is complete.

text.value: The final rite is cutting the hair. Once done, you leave Ihrām — its restrictions are lifted and your ‘Umrah is complete.

kids.n: Trim evenly from all over the head

text.value: Trim evenly from all over the head

props.text: Shaving is better for men and carries the greater reward; trimming evenly is also valid.

kids.n: Gather the hair and cut about 1–2 cm from the ends. Women never shave.

text.value: Gather the hair and cut about 1–2 cm from the ends. Women never shave.

props.description: Shave the whole head (ḥalq) or trim evenly from all over it (taqṣīr). Shaving is better.
props.title: For men

props.description: Cut about a fingertip’s length from the ends of the hair; shaving is not permitted for women.
props.title: For women

props.description: Exit with the left foot first and say the du‘ā for leaving the masjid.
props.title: Leaving the Masjid

props.description: All Ihrām restrictions are now lifted — perfume, normal clothing, cutting nails and the rest.
props.title: Out of Ihrām

kids.n: Leaving the masjid · left foot first

text.value: Leaving the masjid · left foot first

props.translation: “In the name of Allāh, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allāh. O Allāh, I ask You of Your bounty.”
props.transliteration: Bismillāh, was-salātu was-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhumma innī asʾaluka min fadlik.
props.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ

props.text: May Allāh accept your ‘Umrah, forgive your sins and keep you firm upon Islām.

kids.n: You have finished Saʿī but can’t find a barber. Are you out of Ihrām yet?

text.value: You have finished Saʿī but can’t find a barber. Are you out of Ihrām yet?

kids.n: For men, how do shaving and trimming compare?

text.value: For men, how do shaving and trimming compare?

props.text: Trimming is required; shaving is disliked
Both are valid, but shaving is better
Shaving is only for older pilgrims

props.explanation: The Prophet made du‘ā three times for those who shaved and once for those who trimmed (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī).
props.title: Correct — +1 insight

kids.n: Answers never block you — you can revisit any stage.

props.arabic: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ، وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنقَلِبُونَ
props.note: When to recite: as your journey begins, after saying “Allāhu Akbar” three times. The full travel du‘ā continues in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim.
props.translation: “Glory be to the One who has placed this at our service; we could never have done it ourselves. And to our Lord we will surely return.”
props.title: When Setting Out on a Journey
props.transliteration: Subḥānalladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahū muqrinīn, wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn.

props.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
props.note: When to recite: stepping into any masjid — including Al-Masjid Al-Ḥarām — with the right foot first.
props.translation: “In the name of Allāh, and prayers and peace be upon the Messenger of Allāh. O Allāh, open for me the doors of Your mercy.”
props.title: Upon Entering the Masjid
props.transliteration: Bismillāh, waṣ-ṣalātu was-salāmu ʿalā Rasūlillāh. Allāhumma-ftaḥ lī abwāba raḥmatik.

props.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
props.note: When to recite: in every circuit of Ṭawāf, between the Yemeni corner and the Black Stone.
props.translation: “Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.”
props.title: Between the Yemeni Corner & Black Stone
props.transliteration: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanatan wa fil-ākhirati ḥasanatan wa qinā ʿadhāban-nār.

props.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّكَ عَفُوٌّ تُحِبُّ الْعَفْوَ فَاعْفُ عَنِّي
props.note: When to recite: taught for Laylat al-Qadr, and beautiful at any time — in Ṭawāf, Sa‘ī and every du‘ā.
props.translation: “O Allāh, You are the Pardoner and You love to pardon, so pardon me.”
props.title: Seeking Allāh’s Pardon
props.transliteration: Allāhumma innaka ʿafuwwun tuḥibbul-ʿafwa faʿfu ʿannī.
